message.content:
In Blackjack, an Ace is a “flexible” card that can be counted as either **1** or **11**, depending on which value gives the hand the best chance of winning without busting.  

- **If counting it as 11 keeps the total ≤ 21, you’ll usually treat it as 11.**  
- **If counting it as 11 would bust the hand, you’ll treat it as 1.**  

This flexibility allows you to keep a strong hand while avoiding a bust. For example:

| Hand | Total if Ace = 11 | Total if Ace = 1 | Best value |
|------|-------------------|------------------|------------|
| Ace + 9 | 20 | 10 | 20 |
| Ace + 10 | 21 | 11 | 21 (Blackjack) |
| Ace + 9 + 3 | 23 (bust) | 13 | 13 |

If you have more than one Ace, you can treat one as 11 and the rest as 1 (or all as 1) to avoid busting. For instance, Ace + Ace + 9 can be 21 (11 + 1 + 9) or 11 (1 + 1 + 9).  

So the rule is simple: **An Ace counts as 11 unless that would cause the hand to exceed 21, in which case it counts as 1.**
